summary.one_liner: Pixie is an open-source, eBPF-based observability tool for Kubernetes applications that gives service maps, resource metrics, full-body request traces, and profiling without manual instrumentation.
summary.what_it_does: Pixie uses eBPF to automatically collect telemetry from Kubernetes clusters, including full-body application requests, resource and network metrics, and application profiles. It stores and queries this data inside the cluster rather than shipping it out. Users query the data with PxL, a Pythonic query language, which can be used from the web-based Live UI, the CLI, or client APIs. The README describes views such as service maps, pod state, flame graphs, DNS and TCP drop/retransmit maps, and per-service latency. It also mentions deploying bpftrace programs across nodes and dynamic logging for Go binaries without recompiling. The README says Pixie uses less than 5% of cluster CPU, and usually under 2%.
use_cases: debug microservice requests in a kubernetes cluster
monitor service latency and error rates
find network traffic and DNS issues between pods
profile CPU usage with flame graphs in kubernetes
monitor database query latency and throughput
debug running Go binaries without redeploying
how_to_run: Install Pixie following the Install Guides linked in the README
notable: Automatic eBPF-based telemetry with no code changes needed
Data is collected and queried in-cluster rather than sent to an external backend
Scriptable via PxL across the UI, CLI, and API
Distributed bpftrace deployment to all cluster nodes
Dynamic Go logging without recompiling or redeploying
caveats: Installation and setup details are only available via linked guides, not in the README itself
Release versions for CLI, Cloud, Vizier, and Operator are versioned separately
keywords: find slow requests in my cluster
